title: Need to know: gas in Winter 2026-27  | Wood Mackenzie
gist: Wood Mackenzie's winter 2026-27 gas outlook says Hormuz LNG disruption has driven TTF above 100 euros/MWh, with European storage near 75% and projected to end winter just 17% full. US associated gas depresses Henry Hub while data centres lift long-run US gas demand.

themes.theme: Middle East disruption and LNG flows

insights.claim: Before the Middle East conflict Asia imported a share of its LNG from Qatar and the UAE; after losing those volumes, buyers scrambled for spot cargoes at elevated prices.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Loss of Gulf LNG is the root of the current price spike in Asia and Europe.
insights.locator: As the impacts of geopolitical events

insights.claim: Gas-to-coal switching in power has cut LNG imports into Japan and South Korea, while oil-product switching is limited by high prices and tight availability.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Coal switching is a demand-side release valve; oil switching is not available now.
insights.locator: Fuel switching has played a key role

insights.claim: Taiwan, Bangladesh and Thailand have few switching options and keep paying premium prices to secure LNG for power generation and fertiliser production.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Inelastic buyers set marginal prices and support spot premiums.
insights.locator: In countries with fewer switching options

insights.claim: Europe and Asia are competing for LNG cargoes, pushing both regions' gas prices to four-year highs and TTF above 100 euros/MWh in late October.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Price rally reflects physical competition for cargoes as European storage injections lag.
insights.quote: TTF breaching the symbolic 100€/MWh threshold in late October
insights.locator: This has triggered a sustained price rally

insights.claim: The pace at which LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz resume and increase is the key determinant of market tightness this winter and into 2027.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Hormuz flow data is the single most important variable to monitor for gas pricing.
insights.locator: The pace at which LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz

themes.theme: Oil market spillover to North American gas

insights.claim: Lost Gulf and Russian oil equals the output of Texas and New Mexico in 2026, and the resulting higher oil prices drove production growth in unaffected regions, especially the US Lower 48.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: High oil prices are pulling US supply growth forward.
insights.locator: Missing oil from the Gulf and Russia

insights.claim: Extra associated gas from oil drilling is pushing down Henry Hub benchmark prices even as global gas is tight.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: US gas decouples from global prices because oil-driven supply is price-insensitive; this widens arbitrage to LNG.
insights.locator: That has led to huge amounts of additional associated gas

insights.claim: Permian gas supply and pipeline capacity should stay fairly well aligned through 2027, but continued oil growth could push flows into pipeline constraints by the end of next year.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Permian takeaway constraints could re-emerge in late 2027, hurting local prices.
insights.locator: We expect Permian gas supply and pipeline capacity growth

themes.theme: US power demand and data centres

insights.claim: US power demand growth is forecast at 3.5% annually over the next decade versus under 1% annually over the past ten years, driven mainly by data centres.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Structural demand shift supports gas generation and gas demand outlook.
insights.locator: From less than 1% annually over the past ten years

insights.claim: Data centres are expected to account for about 25% of total US power demand by 2035, with much supply coming from gas generation.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Links AI buildout directly to US gas demand growth.
insights.locator: The key reason for this dramatic shift

insights.claim: About 100 GW of grid-connected gas generation projects are being tracked to come online over roughly five years, and many data centres are choosing co-located gas generation for speed-to-power.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Behind-the-meter gas adds incremental gas demand beyond the grid-connected pipeline.
insights.locator: We’re currently tracking about 100 gigawatts

insights.claim: European gas storage will be close to 75% full at end-October, well below the five-year range, after summer heatwaves, drought-reduced hydro, warm rivers affecting French nuclear and mothballed coal capacity forced heavy gas reliance.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Low starting storage leaves Europe exposed to cold weather and supply shocks.
insights.locator: European gas storage will be close to 75% full

insights.claim: Fuel switching has already cut European industrial gas demand by almost 20% since 2022, so further large demand reduction would come only at the cost of a recession.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Demand destruction is largely exhausted; the next adjustment would be macro-negative.
insights.locator: Fuel switching has already reduced European industrial gas demand

insights.claim: On current forwards and ten-year normal weather, European storage is expected to end winter only 17% full, with a cold winter taking it lower and creating large upside price risk.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Skew is to the upside for European gas prices; some countries will be hit harder than the average.
insights.locator: we expect European storage to end the winter only 17% full

insights.claim: The average storage figure hides large regional disparities, with some European countries more likely to run short of gas.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Country-level exposure matters for relative trades and policy response.
insights.locator: Beyond this average stock number

insights.claim: El Nino typically brings a warmer, wetter winter to Japan, South Korea and parts of China, which could cut LNG imports into the three countries by up to 2.5 million tonnes and, via rainfall, keep demand lower into spring.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Lower Asian demand would free LNG for Europe's depleted storage and ease prices.
insights.locator: In Asia, El Niño as a weather phenomenon

insights.claim: In the US, one standard deviation in winter temperature equals around 500 Bcf of gas left in storage at end-March, and El Nino correlates with a very mild winter, though its flows tend to keep cold from dropping south rather than eliminating it.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Mild-winter odds are bearish for US gas storage balances and prices.
insights.locator: In the US, El Niño has a strong correlation

themes.theme: Post-winter price path and Hormuz scenarios

insights.claim: Supply shortfall is supporting elevated prices along the forward curve, and Europe is expected to keep attracting marginal LNG cargoes through 2027, keeping prices higher for longer.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Expect backwardation to fade slowly; do not assume a quick post-winter price fall.
insights.locator: The supply shortfall today is supporting elevated prices

insights.claim: If Hormuz flows normalise, oil prices could fall rapidly, improving oil-product competitiveness against gas and increasing fuel switching in some Asian markets.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: A Hormuz reopening is bearish for both oil and gas, with switching amplifying the gas decline.
insights.locator: If flows through the Strait of Hormuz normalise

insights.claim: If Hormuz LNG flows do not return to normal, there would barely be enough gas globally to meet essential Asian demand while refilling European storage to minimum levels before winter 2027/28.
insights.speaker: Randall Collum
insights.so_what: Tail risk of critical tightness; supports long-dated upside exposure.
insights.locator: However, if disruptions persist
